assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and demonstrated with strontium, reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and beat the microwave definition of the second by orders of magnitude. This is the clearest case of a new measurement technique opening new observations: relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and dark-matter searches. It is a decisive demonstration of coherence and linewidth control, which I weigh heavily.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the original lattice-clock proposal and the first Sr realization, and Ye's group (JILA) brought the systematic uncertainty and comparison to record levels. Two laureates is a clean configuration. The credit of the broader frequency-comb and trapped-ion clock community (Hall and Hänsch already prized; Wineland 2012) is acknowledged but separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature. Many independent labs worldwide have reproduced and improved the clocks, and the redefinition of the second is being discussed. Recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to wait for the formal redefinition of the SI second.
Other contributors (e.g. Lemonde, Schiller, Bloom/Ludlow/Campbell in the Ye group) are not in the credited list, so I cannot assess their relative claims from supplied data.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proposals for quantum computation with trapped ions and for atom-based quantum simulation, together with their experimental realisation, created a whole experimental field in AMO physics. The experiments show gates, entanglement and simulation with control I regard as demanding and convincing.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller supplied the foundational theory (ion-trap gate, cold-atom Hubbard simulator); Blatt is the strongest experimental voice for ion-based processing. Bloch is also strong for the simulation side, but the field is a compound of ions and lattices, and four names exceed the limit, so a three-person configuration forces a choice. I choose theory plus ion experiments.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed by many independent groups, and now a technology trajectory. Timely, though Wineland and Haroche (2012) already recognised some of the ion-control foundation, so differentiation from that prize needs care.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with candidates B022 and B029 sharing the same theorists.
Selecting three of four credited names leaves out Bloch and the optical-lattice branch, a contentious split.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turns matter waves into high-precision sensors for gravity, rotation and the fine-structure constant, and underpins tests of the equivalence principle. It is a pure measurement-science advance, with real field and commercial prototypes.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard pioneered atom interferometry with matter-wave gratings, Mlynek's group produced the early Young double-slit and grating experiments with atoms, and Kasevich developed the precision gravimeters and gyroscopes. Chu's cooling-based work was partly recognised in 1997; the distinction between that and this credit needs checking. The three-name configuration seems reasonable but I cannot verify which early demonstration (Keith/Pritchard, Carnal/Mlynek, Kasevich/Chu) has priority.
assessment.maturity: Mature in laboratory sensitivity and increasingly deployed in gravimetry. Space and fundamental-physics applications remain developing, so the full impact is still emerging.
uncertainties: Priority among the early 1991 demonstrations is disputed in my own recollection, and I have not verified it.
Overlap with Chu's cooling contributions and with Cornell/Wieman/Ketterle BEC-based interferometry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single NV centres in diamond gave a room-temperature solid-state qubit and nanoscale sensor for magnetic fields, temperature and electric fields, with uses in biology and materials. This matches my interest in quantum sensors with medical potential.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group and Jelezko demonstrated single-NV optical detection and coherent control; Lukin's group made the sensing and quantum-register proposals and demonstrations. Others (Awschalom, Hanson, Lukin's collaborators Yacoby/Walsworth) are important and absent, so the credited trio may omit key contributors.
assessment.maturity: Single-NV work is replicated worldwide. Practical sensing advantage over competitors in real applications is still partly aspirational.
uncertainties: Large community with overlapping priority claims, so a three-person limit is unavoidable and possibly unfair.
Lukin is also credited in B005, so a double award would be a concern.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-matter interfaces and quantum memories (DLCZ protocol, cavity QED networks, quantum state transfer) are the basic building blocks for quantum repeaters. I know the rare-earth-crystal memory branch of this field well and know how hard efficiency, storage time and fidelity targets are to meet together.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller laid out the theory of quantum state transfer and repeaters; Kimble led the experimental realisation with atoms and cavities. The experimental community that built ensemble memories (including crystal-based memories) is large and not represented in the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Proof-of-principle is established, but a working long-distance quantum network or repeater with a clear advantage is not yet demonstrated, so recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Efficiency, multimode capacity and storage time of memories remain below repeater requirements.
Overlap with B008 and B034 on named theorists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Squeezed light for interferometric precision, from Caves's 1981 proposal to experimental squeezing and its routine use in gravitational-wave detectors, is a concrete case in which a quantum-optics idea improves a real instrument beyond the standard quantum limit.
assessment.attribution: Caves provided the theory, Kimble contributed the early experimental squeezing demonstration, and Schnabel contributed the GEO600 and generation of squeezed light at detector-compatible frequencies. Slusher's and Walls's early squeezing work, plus Mavalvala's LIGO implementation, are also relevant and make the allocation open.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed through operating detectors (GEO600, LIGO, Virgo). The gravitational-wave connection to the 2017 prize makes timing attractive, but the credit is spread over many.
uncertainties: Allocation among Caves, Kimble, Schnabel, Mavalvala and early squeezing experimenters is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting circuits into controllable, readable quantum systems with strong light-matter coupling and dispersive readout. This is the hardware platform behind much current quantum-processor work.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues made the theory proposal, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. The trio is a natural configuration. The 2025 prize recognised macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits to my knowledge, so the committee would have to judge distinctness, which I cannot settle from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and independently confirmed in many labs, but recognition so soon after a closely related prize looks less timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the recent prize on superconducting circuits (I am relying on memory, not verification).
Devoret, Martinis and Nakamura are not in this credited list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing arrays use the extraordinary stability of millisecond pulsars as a galaxy-scale detector. The 2023 evidence for a nanohertz background is a remarkable feat of long-baseline timing precision, although as a measurement it is a first detection with an unsettled origin.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across PPTA, EPTA, NANOGrav, IPTA and CPTA, and the founding ideas (Sazhin, Detweiler, Foster and Backer) are not on the list. Hobbs, Kramer and Siemens represent three collaborations, but any three names are an imperfect proxy.
assessment.maturity: Premature. The signal is evidence rather than a decisive detection, and astrophysical versus cosmological origin is not settled; independent confirmation is still incoming.
uncertainties: Detection significance and the source of the background (supermassive black hole binaries versus new physics).
Allocation across collaborations and the foundational theorists.
